_readme: THE ALLOWLIST. ci-11a. Every command any front end may ever run on this device's behalf is here, by
id, with its argv FIXED. A caller names a verb id and (where the argv has a {placeholder}) a value for
each parameter; nothing else crosses. There is no free-form command, no shell string, no way to append
an argument, and no verb that takes a path.
LAYER BOUNDARY (his rule 2026-09-19 — 'keep different pieces logically separate, like CLI vs JavaFX').
This file is the whole contract between the CLI half and any front end. The CLI half (setup.sh, the
steps, doctor.sh) knows only that an action is `privileged: true` and names a verb id; it contains no
reference to how an elevation is obtained. A front end knows only this file; it never composes a
command of its own. `pol jenkins verbs` prints it, and the selftest proves every action every step
emits names a verb that is here and passes every parameter regex.
PARAMETERS are validated on BOTH sides against the regexes below: by polari-jenkins/setup/protocol.py
before an action is ever offered, and again by whoever executes the verb. An unanchored or absent
regex is a selftest failure, not a permissive default.
A SECRET VALUE NEVER TRAVELS IN ARGV. `stdin: "secret"` means exactly one thing: the executor collects
the value itself and writes it to the command's standard input. It is never a parameter, never part of
a URL, never echoed back, and never appears in the setup protocol document.

init-device.label: Create the system secrets posture (the polari-ci user and /etc/polari-jenkins/secrets), and move anything already in the checkout there
init-device.why_privileged: it creates a system user and a root-owned directory under /etc

secrets-put.label: Store one secret. The VALUE is read from standard input — it is never an argument.
secrets-put.why_privileged: under the system posture the store is root:polari-ci 0640

apt-install-tools.label: Install the host tools the pipeline device needs

docker-group.label: Add a user to the docker group. ⚠ ROOT-EQUIVALENT: a member can start a container that mounts / as root.

wired-up.label: Bring a wired network connection up, by its NetworkManager connection NAME (never an address)

doctor.label: What is configured on this device and what is not — read-only

preflight.label: The resource guard: is the device clear of a Polari/isle installation of its own, and has it the room?

setup-step.label: Recompute one step of the walkthrough

setup-answer.label: Answer ONE question of one step and recompute it. The key is a device.env knob and the value is what the person typed or chose.
setup-answer.note: the sibling of setup-step: same recomputation, one answer written first. A question binds to this verb with "value": "{answer}" — the executor substitutes what the person entered. A SECRET question never binds here: its value goes to secrets-put on stdin, collected by the executor's own prompt, because a secret in an argument is a secret in the process list.

setup-run.label: Run ONE unprivileged action of the walkthrough and return the step it belongs to

up.label: Bring the controller up (through the docker socket — not root)
